newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Police officer held in Murtaza Bhutto killing case.
newsitem.headline: Police officer held in Murtaza Bhutto killing case.

text.p: Pakistani police said on Sunday they had detained Karachi's former deputy inspector general of police, a suspect in the killing of opposition leader Benazir Bhutto's estranged brother, Murtaza.
"Shoaib Suddle has been detained," a senior police officer said, without specifying the reason. "His residence has been declared as a sub-jail after his detention overnight."
Suddle was staying at the Police Club in Karachi's affluent Defence Society suburb.
His detention follows the completion of a judicial inquiry into the death of Murtaza, who was killed with seven companions on September 20 near his home in this southern port city.

The three-member tribunal, set up on October 18 under Justice Nasir Aslam Zahid, a Supreme Court judge, submitted its report to the government on May 31 with a recommendation that its findings be made public. The report has yet to be published.

Police have accused Bhutto's husband Asif Ali Zardari, former chief minister of Sindh province Abdullah Shah, former Intelligence Bureau chief Masood Sharif and 19 police officers, including Suddle, of involvement in Murtaza's murder.

In her testimony to the tribunal, Bhutto said her brother's killing was part of a plot to overthrow her government, which was sacked by President Farooq Leghari on November 5 on disputed charges of corruption and misrule.
Zardari, who has been in a Karachi jail since his wife's dismissal, denies involvement in Murtaza's killing.
